events.title: Earlier July 2025 outburst flood destroyed the Friendship Bridge
events.detail: A glacial lake outburst flood on 8 July 2025 destroyed the Friendship Bridge at Rasuwagadhi. Gyirong County afterwards built flood defences, which the August 2026 flow overwhelmed within minutes.

events.title: Seismic signal at 08:37 NPT recorded as a collapse, not an earthquake
events.detail: A tremor near Rasuwagadhi at 08:20 preceded a signal first catalogued as M4.4 at 08:37 NPT, later revised to Ms 5.2 (GFZ Mw 5.7). USGS concluded the signal was generated by a rock-ice collapse from the Lirung massif, not a prior earthquake. A second landslide followed about three hours later (Ms 4.2).

events.title: Debris flow destroys Gyirong Port and Friendship Bridge
events.detail: From about 08:44 NPT CCTV footage shows destruction at Gyirong Port. The debris flow covered about 20 km in roughly seven minutes with a drop of nearly 3,000 m. Customs facilities and the Friendship Bridge at Rasuwagadhi were swept away; Premier Li Qiang visited Gyirong that day per the Wikipedia compilation.

events.title: Flood enters Bhotekoshi/Trishuli; SMS alerts reach 679,295 residents
events.detail: Upstream stations at Syabrubesi (08:50) and Betrawati (09:20) stopped transmitting. Nepal's hydrology department was informed at 09:00 and SMS alerts went to 679,295 riverbank residents in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan from 09:15. Evacuations began along the Trishuli corridor; the flood passed Muglin and reached Devghat by early afternoon, peaking at 6.57 m at 16:00.

events.title: Nepal activates International Charter; IFRC releases CHF 1 million
events.detail: At Nepal's request the International Charter Space and Major Disasters was activated at 18:13 NPT (UNITAR managing). 14 helicopters and security forces were deployed, free treatment for injured was ordered, and the IFRC released nearly CHF 1 million. About 430 MW of hydropower was knocked out.

events.title: First counts: 165 dead in Nepal, 826 missing; Tibet reports 3 dead, 558 missing
events.detail: Morning figures listed 165 dead and 73 injured in Nepal with 826 missing, including 579 travellers. Tibetan state media reported 3 dead and 558 missing. Al Jazeera later that day reported more than 390 dead and over 1,500 missing combined, with 668 tourists from 34 countries out of contact. Sources disagreed on the missing totals because foreign nationals may be double-counted.

events.title: IFRC launches CHF 25 million appeal; UNICEF cites 17,000 children in need
events.detail: The IFRC opened a 24-month CHF 25 million appeal. UNICEF said at least 17,000 children needed urgent aid, with 18 schools destroyed. Nepal's finance ministry said about NPR 20 billion could be redirected to relief.

events.title: Prime Minister visits Nuwakot; authorities warn a barrier lake could burst
events.detail: Prime Minister Balen Shah visited Nuwakot. Chinese authorities warned that a barrier lake of about 2 million m³ could breach and flood downstream areas again.

events.title: Barrier lake overflows slightly; rescues halted for about three hours
events.detail: A reported breach paused rescues for about three hours. Officials later said water rose about 0.6 m and risk eased; the lake was largely drained by 30 August. The IFRC said it was very concerned about a secondary flood.

events.title: Nepal toll reaches 579; missing rises to 1,924 after hydropower workers added
events.detail: Nepal's toll rose to 579 and missing to 1,924 after 933 hydropower workers were added to the list. About 14,829 security personnel were mobilised. Seven bodies were reported recovered in rivers in India. The UN cited 538 recovered bodies and about 3,750 rescued earlier in the day. Nepal said it did not currently need foreign search teams.

events.title: First foreign aid pledges: South Korea, China, World Bank
events.detail: South Korea pledged US$1 million, China pledged immediate cash aid and the World Bank said up to Rs 25 billion could be mobilised. About 90 Americans were unaccounted for. WHO warned of disease risk from displacement.

events.title: India evacuates thousands in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand
events.detail: India evacuated thousands from river districts as levels rose. Bodies were later carried about 250 km, with recoveries at Nawalparasi in Nepal and Kushinagar and Maharajganj in Uttar Pradesh.

era: Search, Burials and Tunnel Rescue (29 Aug – 7 Sep)

events.title: NDRRMA reports 616–626 dead across eight districts; Chitwan hardest hit
events.detail: Chitwan recorded the most deaths (233). About 2,500 people were evacuated. Tibet reported 7 dead and 554 missing. About 350 people were rescued from Trishuli 3A but over 100 remained trapped in a tunnel.

sources.name: Wikipedia timeline (citing NDRRMA, Nepal Police)

events.title: China flies 50 tonnes of supplies on two Y-20 aircraft; new flood warnings
events.detail: China sent 50 tonnes of supplies, US$2 million in government aid and US$200,000 from the Red Cross Society of China. Flood warnings were reissued after upstream flow increased; the barrier lake was largely drained.

events.title: Over 250 bodies wash up in Chitwan; mass burials begin
events.detail: More than 250 bodies reached Chitwan and only nine could be readily identified. Mass burials started in Bharatpur. Lack of cold storage later led to 1,044 temporary burials by 26 September.

events.title: China closes Tatopani crossing; controlled blast at Upper Trishuli 3A
events.detail: Tatopani crossing closed on 31 August, leaving Korala the only open crossing. A controlled explosion was carried out at the Upper Trishuli 3A tunnel to reach trapped workers.

events.title: NDRRMA: 1,003 dead, about 4,000 missing, nearly 12,000 rescued
events.detail: Nepal's disaster authority reported 1,003 dead and about 4,000 missing. Ministry of Health said only about 4% of roughly 900 bodies found had been identified. China sent a second aid batch with drones and DNA equipment.

events.title: Makeshift road to Gyirong Port completed; 1.6 million affected
events.detail: China completed a temporary road to Gyirong Port and installed a 4G/5G base station. NDRRMA put the affected population at about 1.6 million.

events.title: Two survivors rescued from Upper Trishuli 3A tunnel; third on 5 September
events.detail: Two workers were rescued on 4 September and a Chinese national the next day. Australian tunnel expert Arnold Dix described it as the toughest rescue of his career.

events.title: China hosts foreign journalists in the rescue area amid censorship reports
events.detail: Foreign journalists were restricted to supervised trips. Reports said videos and eyewitness accounts from Tibet were censored and at least 10 people were penalised for misleading posts. Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said the disaster should not be used for smear campaigns.

events.title: National day of mourning in Nepal
events.detail: Nepal observed a national mourning day. The Army estimated 121 workers still trapped at Upper Trishuli on 7 September.

events.title: Seven-member expert panel formed to investigate cause
events.detail: The government formed a seven-member panel to investigate the cause. Satellite analysis cited a roughly 0.2 km² block falling about 1.2 km, with glacier creep accelerating in the weeks before. The exact date of formation is approximate in the source compilation.

events.detail: Chinese figures for Gyirong stood at 43 dead and 519 missing, including 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries. The International Campaign for Tibet said Tibetan casualties exceeded official numbers.

events.title: Nepal Police last bulletin: 1,454 recovered, 4,718 missing
events.detail: Nepal Police's last published bulletin (30 September) listed 1,454 recovered and 4,718 missing. Secondary analyses noted the search was effectively called off and that nearly 1,000 names were added through bookkeeping rather than new losses.

events.detail: By 1 October only 112 bodies had been identified, versus roughly 900 recovered in the first week, using DNA sampling and photo databases. Some families objected on religious grounds.

events.title: Cabinet proposes cutting legal-death wait for the missing from 12 years to 45 days
events.detail: The proposal needs a presidential ordinance. The PM's relief fund reached NPR 17.06 billion (about US$110 million) with NPR 1 billion disbursed. Nepal Cabinet figures that day listed 1,455 dead.

events.detail: Nepal damage estimated at NPR 277.79 billion (US$1.8 bn), losses NPR 136.27 billion and reconstruction NPR 723.67 billion (US$4.78 bn). ADB cut Nepal's growth forecast from 4.5% to 4.1% and the World Bank to 3.7%. Exact publication date of the assessment is approximate.
